record.title: Canine Babesiosis: Epidemiological and Clinical Features
record.abstract:
Babesiosis is a cosmopolitan disease produced by blood parasites Babesia, a genus of protozoal piroplasms and transmitted by ticks bites. In Europe canine babesiosis is produced by two species of protoazoals, Babesia canis and Babesia gibsoni that are very different by phenotype and genotype. Clinical signs vary depending on the species or subspecies that are involved. This study presents epidemiological and clinical aspects of the disease from the south part of the country.
	The study had been performed from January to December 2008 in the Clinics of The Faculty of Veterinary Medicine Bucharest, on a number of 508 suspected dogs. Suspicion was based on the clinical signs. Ticks had been discovered on the skin of the animals during examination proceeded by the doctors in the clinics or by the owners. Blood samples had been microscopically examined after MGG coloration, with an immersion objective. In parallel the identification of the ticks had been performed.

screening.species: B. canis and B. gibsoni (suspected, smear only)
screening.rationale: Based on the abstract (the DOI and journal landing pages returned 404 and 403). It is a 2008 clinic series of 508 suspected dogs that reports 'clinical aspects', but it does not say whether clinical sign frequencies or laboratory host data for the confirmed cases are given.
